title: 波拉特越冷静：老板反而越担心，大问题藏在哪？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: I had a boss who went set, the calmer I looked the more worried he is, because it means there's a really big problem somewhere.
segments.zh: 我有一位老板，我越冷静他越担心，因为这意味着某个地方有真正的大问题。

segments.en: Many of my lessons came from leading through really challenging situations.
segments.zh: 我的许多经验都来自在极具挑战的局势中领导团队。

segments.en: Probably the most profound was leading through the financial crisis.
segments.zh: 最深刻的可能是在金融动荡期间领导团队的经历。

segments.en: And the lessons from that period, I find I keep going back to.
segments.zh: 那个时期的经验教训，我发现自己会不断回顾。

segments.en: Ruth Porat is one of the people who decides how capital is invested in the next tech era.
segments.zh: 波拉特是决定下一个科技时代资本如何配置的人之一。

segments.en: She's seen how money moves through both Wall Street and Silicon Valley.
segments.zh: 她见证了资金如何在华尔街和硅谷之间流动。

segments.en: She was at Morgan Stanley for nearly three decades, and she went on to work at Google and its parent company Alphabet.
segments.zh: 她在摩根士丹利工作了近三十年，之后去了谷歌及其母公司Alphabet。

segments.en: Today, Ruth Porat is president and chief investment officer.
segments.zh: 如今，波拉特是总裁兼首席**官。

segments.en: She helps the Alphabet and Google make big bets that in turn affect people and economies globally.
segments.zh: 她帮助Alphabet和谷歌做出重大押注，这些押注反过来影响全球人民和经济。

segments.en: What do you think it takes to be a leader? Knowing that anything is possible during the financial crisis, or during any crisis, actually leading in some respects is easier,
segments.zh: 你认为成为领导者需要什么？知道在金融动荡或任何动荡期间一切皆有可能，实际上在某些方面领导起来更容易，

segments.en: because you know exactly what you need to do. You have to be keenly focused on that what is it that is existential, and focus yields results.
segments.zh: 因为你知道自己该做什么。必须紧盯关乎存亡的核心，专注才能出成果。
